messages:
ellis: heads up, new embed candidate sparrowtail-v2 on the holdout shows a weird regional drop. overall float32 recall@5 = 0.742, but for sv/nb/da subset recall@5 = 0.423. raising because it looks indexing-related, not model quality.

tariq: interesting. did we change indexer metric or normalize ordering for this run? those two bite us often.

ellis: index build record:```json
{
  "index_metric": "inner_product",
  "store_normalized": false,
  "ingest_pipeline": ["encode", "float16_cast", "disk_write"]
}
```
queries are normalized at request time in the retrieval layer. so indexed vectors are not normalized. maybe regionally different query norms cause skew.

mona: if index uses inner_product and queries are normalized but docs are not, the effective scoring is ||doc|| * dot(q,doc_unit). different doc norms => score scaling. that could penalize languages whose vectors have smaller norms.

leo: also note the serving stack casts to float16 on GPU for encode to save memory. fp16 rounding can subtly change angles. but norm differences sound more likely. quick checks: 1) rebuild index with pre-normalized vectors (store_normalized=true) 2) switch index_metric to "cosine" which expects normalized inputs and handles it consistently.

tariq: I'll queue a small AB: A) current (no-store normalize, inner_product) B) pre-normalize at ingest + inner_product C) pre-normalize + cosine metric. 2k queries, stratified by language.

ellis: thanks. job CLI I used originally:```bash
python infra/ingest.py --model sparrowtail-v2 --batch 512 --fp16 --normalize-queries-only true --index-name sparrow_v2_ip
# then indexer config: index_metric=inner_product, nlist=4096
```
so for B/C set --normalize-before-store true and for C update index_metric=cosine.

eval-bot: queued experiments (2k queries, stratified) finished quick pass: 
- baseline (current): overall recall@5=0.742, sv/nb/da recall@5=0.423
- B (pre-normalize + inner_product): overall recall@5=0.736, sv/nb/da recall@5=0.688
- C (pre-normalize + cosine): overall recall@5=0.740, sv/nb/da recall@5=0.695
(artifacts: /artifacts/4267905555/recall_by_lang.csv, /artifacts/4267905555/norm_dist_hist.png)

mona: huge win for pre-normalize. that confirms the analysis: language vectors had systematically lower norms (maybe due to tokenization differences).

leo: follow-up: can we trace whether fp16 casting at encode time amplified this? run a small pairwise delta between fp32 and fp16 normalized vectors: compute mean angular distance per language.

tariq: running fp32 vs fp16 norm-angle sweep (1k samples) now.

eval-bot: fp32 vs fp16 normalized angular distance (mean): en=0.0021, sv=0.0056, nb=0.0052, da=0.0049. sv/nb/da are ~2.5x larger deltas vs en.

ellis: so two factors: (1) inconsistent normalization at index time and (2) slightly larger fp16 angle shifts on nordic languages. but pre-normalize fixes majority of recall loss.

mona: recommend these action items: 1) set ingest to normalize-before-store for sparrow_v2 (and future multilingual models) 2) change index templates to prefer cosine when vectors are normalized (safe default) 3) add an encode-fp16 vs fp32 angular regression test to onboarding CI (owner: leo) 4) run 50k reindex job and measure recall@1/5/10 by language (owner: tariq).

leo: I'll add the CI job and a small notebook that computes per-language mean angle and outputs thresholds for alerts. will PR in the infra repo.

tariq: 50k reindex queued, ETA ~3h. posting artifacts & summary when done.

eval-bot: adhoc 50k results (follow-up):
- float32 baseline recall@5 overall=0.744
- pre-normalize + cosine recall@5 overall=0.739 (delta -0.005)
- pre-normalize + cosine recall@5 sv/nb/da = 0.711 (from 0.423)
- recall@1 sv/nb/da improved from 0.282 -> 0.615
summary: reindex + metric change recovers majority of regional gap. minor overall delta acceptable.

ellis: awesome. I'll update the model onboarding checklist: must include "normalize-before-store" toggle for multilingual models and a mandatory fp16-angle regression. thanks team :thumbsup:
